body:
So, from my stand point, Godot needs:

- Fix `JSON` to support inner classes.
- An API to get the declared class name from an Object, with support inner classes. Then `JSON` can use this for serialization. Plus it will allow you to get the name without resourcing to serialization at all. *We have `get_class`, but that gives us the built-in class, which is not what we want*.
- An API to go from the declared class to an script or a constructor or something that can be used for deserialization. Which then `JSON` can use to deserialize. *For me, `get_global_name` solved an important code path, but I'm still populating a dictionary from `ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list()` to be able to go from the name to the script to be able to create an instance in my custom serialization code, and I can't support inner classes either.*

Hello, I am now facing the same issue: I need to determine the name of an inner class from a given object.
I wanted to start replacing deprecated methods such as “inst_to_dict,” but there is no option to obtain the class name of an inner class.

@dalexeev So when will the function `inst_to_dict` be deleted, and what is the alternative to it?
The specified functions  `JSON.from_native() or Object.get_property_list()` do not return an inner class name.

Using `obj.get_property_list()` misses the class name
`{ "name": "Built-in script", "class_name": &"", "type": 0, "hint": 0, "hint_string": "", "usage": 128 }`

I tried different ways no success, only `inst_to_dict` gives me the script path and real class name.

```
			prints("--inst_to_dict----------------------------")
			prints(inst_to_dict(obj))
			prints("--var_to_str----------------------------")
			prints(var_to_str(obj))
			prints("--from_native----------------------------")
			prints(JSON.from_native(obj, true))
			prints("--get_property_list ----------------------------")
			prints(obj.get_property_list())
```

> So when will the function `inst_to_dict` be deleted, and what is the alternative to it? I don't remember a single case in 4.x where we removed functionality that was declared deprecated. Especially when there is no alternative. The "deprecated" status means that we consider this functionality unnecessary/incorrect and most likely will not update it or fix the existing problems with it. We already have several core methods of text and binary serialization, having another one in GDScript seems redundant and unjustified. I don't know when we will introduce new and better thought-out functionality for reflection and serialization. This is partly due to the lack of a unified type system, representation of class/type information and a single API regardless of the type. Currently, the APIs for different types are very disjoint and incomplete: * Global constants, enumerations and functions - there are internal APIs that are not available in GDScript. * Built-in `Variant` types - there are internal APIs that are not available in GDScript. * Native and `GDExtension` classes - `ClassDB`. * GDScript classes - Some information is available via `GDScript` and `Script` classes. * Global scripts - Can be listed via `ProjectSettings.get_global_class_list()`. * Unnamed scripts, autoload singletons - More or less supported, but there are some cases where a named class is required. * Inner and runtime classes - Cannot be serialized, as they do not have a resource path, and core does not have a unified FQCN/FQTN. * Built-in scripts - Only supported, have many limitations. Core API `Object.get_{property,method,signal}_list()` provides some reflection, but it is not unified enough. Inner, runtime, and built-in scripts are not represented in a universal unified form (no FQCN/FQTN), `hint_string` is empty for them: Although it could be something like `res://run.gd::InnerClass`. But before adding this, we must be sure that the format is well-defined, universal and used the same way everywhere. (Also, I'm not sure if this entry is available in release builds.)

@dalexeev thanks for your answer.

Ok, I'm fine when the deprecated function will not be deleted.
But `get_property_list` is current not an alternative because using on the inner class instance there is no info about the parent class script or class name.
On my execution context i have only the inner class instance and no reference to the parent.
